I hold all my useful utilities in a util.pl file. I then include it into the program like this: require '/full/path/to/util.pl';

Here's a list of the routines, followed by the code for them.

  • $n=Commafy($n); # Add commas to number.
  • $s=dropquote($s); # Drops ONLY leading and trailing double quotes, if any. Useful when reading Excel data that contains commas.
  • $n=getdata($a[$i], 'defval');
  • $dt=getfulldatetime(); # Used with naming log or output files. Returns date in format YYYYMMDD-hhmmss.
  • $s=trim($s); # Remove leading and trailing spaces from a string.
  • @a=trimarr(\@); # Trim every entry in an array.
  • @a=uniquearr(@a); # Disallow any dupe entries in array. 
#################################################################
# Add thousands separators to a number. WORKS
# In: a string representing a number.
# Out: a number formatted with commas (US) if needed.
sub Commafy
{my $text = reverse $_[0];
$text =~ s/(\d\d\d)(?=\d)(?!\d*\.)/$1,/g;
return scalar reverse $text;

} # Commafy
################################################################# 
# Drop first and last dbl quote marks. Used to clean up Excel ascii data.
# In: string with possible dbl quotes on front and rear.
# Out: string without dbl quotes.
sub dropquote
{my($l)=@_;
my($s,$t,$le,@a,@b,$i,$j,$procname);

$procname="dropquote";

if (!(defined $l))
 {
 $s='';
 }
else {
 $s=$l;
 }
$le=len($s);
if ($s=~m/^".+"$/)
 {
 $s=substr($s,1,$le-2); # Get middle of string w/o quotes.
 }

return $s; # dropquote
}
#################################################################
# If $l is defined, return it. Else return default value of $defval.
# When dealing with data in arrays (returned from an SQL statement) I often
# deal with undefined values. This is a routine to deal with undef values. 
sub getdata
{my($l,$defval)=@_;
my($s,$t,@a,@b,$i,$j,$procname);

$procname="getdata";
if ((defined $l) and (len($l)>0))
 {
 return $l;
 }
else {
 return $defval;
 }

return ''; # getdata
}
###########################################################################
# July 2014
# Return date in format: YYMMDD-hhmmss. Used on filenames.
# Does not require POSIX;
sub getfulldatetime
{
#my($l)=@_;
my(@a,@b,$i,$j,$procname,$s,$t);
my($day,$mo,$sec,$year,$hr);

$procname="getfulldatetime";
@a=localtime();
$day=sprintf("%02d",$a[3]);
$mo=sprintf("%02d",$a[4]+1); # Month is 0-11.

($sec,$min,$hr,$day, $mo, $year) = (localtime)[0,1,2,3,4,5];
$year=sprintf("%04d",$year);
$mo = sprintf '%02d', $mo+1;
$day = sprintf '%02d', $day;
$s= ($year+1900).$mo.$day;
$s.="-".sprintf("%02d",$hr).sprintf("%02d",$min).sprintf("%02d",$sec);

return $s; # getfulldatetime
}
#################################################################
# Removes trailing and leading whitespace, not just spaces, but tabs too.
# Call: $s=trim($t);
sub trim
{my($uul)=@_;
if (defined($uul))
 {
 $uul=~s/^\s+//;
 $uul=~s/\s+$//;
 }
return $uul;
} # trim

###########################################################################
# Trim all entries in array.
# Calling: @arr=trimarr(\@arr);
# In: array
# Out: array
sub trimarr
{my($arr)=@_;
my(@a,@b,$i,$j,$procname,$s,$t);

$procname="trimarr";

@a=@$arr;
@b=();
foreach $t (@a)
 {
 if ( (defined($t)) )
 {
 $t=trim($t);
 }
 else {
 $t=''; # For undefined element.
 }
 push(@b,$t);
 } # foreach
return @b; # trimarr
}

####################################################################
# Return array of unique values.
# In: Array
# Out: Array of unique values, sorted.
# Calling: @b=uniquearr(@a);
sub uniquearr
{
#my($l)=@_;
my(@a,@b,$i,$j,$procname);

$procname="uniquearr";

return sort(keys(%{{map{$_ => 1}@_}}));

return; # uniquearr
}
